clue.text: Phone about passage out — and going back

indicators.note: about means the phone word goes round the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to phone someone is to ring them
an egress is a way out, a passage leading outside

explanation.surface: Someone calls about a corridor exit while heading back.
explanation.definitionFit: Regressing means returning to an earlier state, a backward movement.

clue.text: Forced to turn up in Holland

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word made from bottom to top

parts.note: made means forced, as in made to do it

explanation.surface: Someone compelled to appear in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a town in North Holland, famous for its cheese.

clue.text: Report sappers delayed

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, RE, are known as sappers
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A news item that the army engineers are running late.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to tell or recount events.

clue.text: A light boat will work

parts.note: shall is an auxiliary like will
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A small craft will do the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallop is a light open boat for shallow waters.

clue.text: One's going round the church, so gets chilled

indicators.note: going round says the first piece surrounds the church

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I plus S
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man circling the church outside gets cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice is to freeze or make very cold.

clue.text: Escape a wag, yet appear put out

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A joker manages to flee while seeming annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight or escape, as by robbers.

clue.text: Over-age employee, skilful and easy to deal with

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the employee word sits above the age word

parts.note: a man is a worker or hand
taken as written
able means skilful

explanation.surface: An older worker who is competent and easy to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manageable can be controlled or handled without difficulty.

clue.text: Camping with the head makes for diligence

parts.note: someone camping is in a tent
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Going camping with the boss promotes hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Intentness is close concentrated application to a task.

clue.text: Green 'rule: never start!

parts.note: a law is a rule laid down

indicators.note: start asks for only the opening letter of the word never

explanation.surface: A stern notice on a bowling green forbidding anyone ever to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is a stretch of mown grass, a green such as one for bowls.

clue.text: Alarm inept characters effect reform at Westminster

indicators.note: the letters (characters) of the preceding words undergo a reform, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alarmingly incompetent group pushes through changes in British government.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK legislature sits in the Palace of Westminster, so Westminster stands for it.

clue.text: Having taken food outside, are going back inside to make pop

indicators.note: outside says the eating word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to have taken food is to have eaten, past tense ate

indicators.note: going back means the word are is read from right to left

explanation.surface: After a meal outdoors, people go back in to make fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns ARE into ERA, which sits inside ATE; 'inside' merely restates the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate a drink is to charge it with gas so it becomes fizzy soda.

clue.text: Red rose arrangement at the back of the altar

definitions.text: at the back of the altar

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters, like flowers, sets them in a new order

explanation.surface: A floral display of red roses placed behind a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen standing behind a church altar.

clue.text: No relative may make such a telling statement

indicators.note: may make suggests the letters can be turned into something new

explanation.surface: A disclosure that one has no family connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a disclosure, a surprising and telling thing made known.

clue.text: Topping property with growth-potential

parts.note: a building's top surface where plants can be grown, topping in the sense of on top

explanation.surface: An excellent investment property with room to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants grow in a garden made on a flat building top.

clue.text: Edged weapon for a brother in the Kent area

indicators.note: in says the brother group sits inside the area

parts.note: Kent is in SE, the south-east of England

explanation.surface: A sword for a monk living in a south-eastern county.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a curved cavalry sword with a cutting edge.

clue.text: If a stranger gets in the way it's noticeable

indicators.note: gets in says the stranger is placed inside the word for the way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an alien is a stranger or foreigner

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar person standing in the road is easy to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or standing out, so readily noticed.

clue.text: Not moving yet

explanation.surface: Stationary even so.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless is one sense; nevertheless or up to now is the other.

clue.text: The reception of like-minded people?

parts.note: a social reception for guests, and also a political group of people sharing the same views

explanation.surface: A gathering where everyone thinks alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a social gathering and a political faction of the same opinions.

clue.text: None left after six-play on this…

indicators.note: after places the words for none and left behind the number six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A game with six players leaves no one to play the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A viol is an early bowed stringed instrument that a musician plays.

clue.text: … and on this when setting the ring in order

indicators.note: in says the ring is placed inside the order

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: play this instrument while arranging the ring neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link to the previous clue, so the definition borrows its 'play': an instrument to play on.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, something one plays music on.

clue.text: Note the record is amusing

parts.note: D is a musical note
a roll is an official list or register, a record

explanation.surface: A remark that the register is entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means wryly funny or comic.

clue.text: Leaves large areas short of water

explanation.surface: Someone departs from vast arid regions.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is one sense; arid wastelands such as the Sahara the other.

clue.text: Stay till the end, taking many a drink

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals, a large number
stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Remaining at the bar until closing, downing plenty of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure or survive until a finish.

clue.text: The heir will have an entry in general

indicators.note: in says the entry is placed inside the general

parts.note: Robert E Lee was a Confederate general
a gate is an entrance or way in

explanation.surface: Someone's heir is named in a general's will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee receives a legacy under a will, a kind of heir.

clue.text: Steps the novice totters up

parts.note: L is the learner plate for a novice
people who tot up figures are adders

explanation.surface: A beginner wobbles as he climbs the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totters' looks like wobbling, but read it as tot-ters, people who tot up sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladders are sets of rungs or steps for climbing.

clue.text: It's unusual in the German to falter

indicators.note: in says the unusual word is placed inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
odd means unusual

explanation.surface: Something strange happening in Germany makes someone hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter or move shakily, as through age.

clue.text: Weary about commercial invective

indicators.note: about means the weary word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to weary is to tire
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone fed up launches into a rant about advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a burst of verbal abuse.

clue.text: Like first-class return from the continent

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: return means the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Travelling back first class from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: Some clean ones should be supplied soon

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fresh supplies of clean items will arrive shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'should be supplied soon' as definition; 'should be supplied' is link padding, and only 'soon' means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Making answer, he makes the odd person dimple

indicators.note: odd suggests the word person is strange, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow, a dimple

explanation.surface: In replying, a man says he dimples the strange individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A respondent is one who replies, especially in a survey or lawsuit.

clue.text: Warning addressed to males only?

parts.note: O is the vocative exclamation used when addressing someone
men are males

explanation.surface: A caution aimed at men alone?
explanation.walkthrough: 'O men!' is how one would address a group of males, the old vocative O.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent warning of what is to come.

clue.text: Give voice about concern — but not a lot

indicators.note: about means the voice word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
a matter is a concern or affair

explanation.surface: Speak out about a worry, but only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount, a slight knowledge.
